data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Salyut 1 was the first space station in history — launched in April 1971, two years ahead of America's Skylab, and the moment the Soviet Union turned its lead in endurance into a permanent presence in orbit. Its triumph was also its tragedy: the first crew to live aboard it, Soyuz 11, died during their return when a valve vented their cabin to vacuum, and the station was never occupied again. It proved a station could be built and reached — and, at the highest cost, taught the lesson that reshaped every crewed spacecraft after it.

The world’s first space station — launched 1971, occupied for 23 days by the Soyuz 11 crew (Dobrovolski, Volkov, Patsayev), all of whom died on return when their capsule depressurised. Salyut 1 was deorbited later that year.
First Almaz military station — depressurised on orbit before any crew arrived; reentered 1973-05-28 after 54 days
Second Almaz military station — Soyuz 14 crew Jul 1974; Soyuz 15 failed automatic docking; reportedly tested an onboard cannon 1975-01-24
Civilian DOS-4 station — hosted Soyuz 17 (29 days) + Soyuz 18 (63 days, then-longest spaceflight) crews; deorbited 1977-02-03
Last Almaz military station — Soyuz 21 + Soyuz 24 crews; Soyuz 23 failed approach; reentered 1977-08-08 after 412 days
